platform.name: NYC In Focus Platform
platform.description: Four-layer architecture for the NYC In Focus live event map, geo-verified ZIP Code community chat, NYC In Focus editorial story feed, and cross-platform mobile applications.
platform.note: Architecture V1 is a planning artifact only. No component, integration point, or service boundary listed here is authorized for implementation without separate explicit authorization.

layers.name: Layer 1 — Data and Editorial Pipeline
layers.description: Ingestion, normalization, stable identity, GPS quality, review, and publishing. The only layer authorized to write to the production event store.

layers.name: Layer 2 — App-Facing API
layers.description: Versioned, read-only endpoints for events, nearby search, event significance, and editorial content. Reads from the production event store; never writes to it.

layers.name: Layer 3 — Account and Community Services
layers.description: Authentication, privacy-preserving geofence verification, ZIP room authorization, real-time chat, moderation, and push notifications. Chat store and private user records are never in any public repository.

layers.name: Layer 4 — Presentation
layers.description: NYC In Focus website (active), iOS and Android applications, editorial feed, widgets, newsletter, and future partner integrations.

components.name: Source Ingestion
components.description: Scheduled pulls from NYC Open Data permit feeds, city agency sources, and additional tracked origins. Output is a normalized candidate set. No production write is authorized during ingestion.
components.notes: Milestones 1–5 established the ingestion foundation. Milestone 6 GPS quality layer is complete/merged on PR #143 (head 5197bdd3918fd95a381e8f9e520681fa7fe36464; merge 8796d64ea628007327e715f0995c16e6ab071c78).

components.name: Normalization and Identity
components.description: Assigns stable event identities, deduplicates records, and applies consistent field normalization across all sources. One canonical shared implementation is the Milestone 7 objective.
components.notes: Milestone 7 will consolidate divergent normalization logic, add explicit duplicate-key signaling, and deprecate unsafe positional review arrays. Separate authorization required.

components.name: GPS and Location Quality
components.description: Validates and resolves GPS coordinates for all events before staging. Includes location-drift detection and identity-transition tests. Raw ingestion coordinates are never exposed in the public API or application.
components.notes: Implementation complete and merged on PR #143 in the live-feeds repository. Milestone 7 remains planned, not authorized, and not started.

components.name: Review and Adjudication
components.description: Operator workflow that stages events for human or rule-based review before any publication. Approve, hold, and reject decisions are recorded with evidence. No automated publication is authorized without a completed review step.
components.notes: The field desk admin dashboard provides read-only operator visibility. Write controls are not in scope for the admin dashboard.

components.name: Publishing Controls
components.description: Gate-controlled publication from staging to the production event store. No code change in any other layer may trigger a publication event. Each publish requires separate explicit authorization.
components.notes: GPS and identity milestones (6 and 7) must complete before the next authorized publish cycle.

components.name: Events API
components.description: Versioned endpoints for event lists, single-event detail, date range queries, and borough and category filters. Includes pagination cursor, caching strategy, rate limits, and a defined error contract.
components.notes: No implementation authorized. Breaking API changes require a new version; existing clients must not be broken.

components.name: Nearby Search
components.description: Geospatial endpoint accepting a center coordinate and radius, returning events within that boundary. Must never expose other users' coordinates, addresses, movement history, or precise distances.
components.notes: No implementation authorized. Response must never include other users' precise coordinates in any form.

components.name: Event Significance Service
components.description: Computes Gold, Silver, and Bronze event significance tiers from evidence signals: estimated and historical attendance, event duration, permit footprint, route and road closures, agencies involved, geographic footprint, and annual flagship status. Tiers cannot be purchased.
components.notes: No implementation authorized. Users must be able to view why an event received its tier. Commercial relationships have no influence on tier computation.

components.name: Articles and Media API
components.description: Exposes NYC In Focus editorial content — articles, galleries, video, and breaking updates — with borough and category facets, map pin deep links, local room deep links, and required content-type labels. Editorial, community, and sponsored content must be visibly distinct.
components.notes: No implementation authorized. WordPress integration is a separate concern in Milestone 13. Content-type labels are required in every response.

components.name: Authentication
components.description: Account creation, login, session management, and password handling. Account identity is separate from location identity. A user does not need an account to browse the map or read local rooms.
components.notes: No implementation authorized. Initial release does not require social login. Location eligibility is a separate service.

components.name: Privacy-Preserving Geofence Verification
components.description: Server-side point-in-polygon check against ZIP Code boundary polygons. Returns only a boolean eligibility decision and a short-lived authorization token. Coordinates are never returned to the caller, stored beyond the request, or exposed to other users. Client-side polygon checks are not acceptable.
components.notes: No implementation authorized. Server must not return coordinates to the caller. Movement history and precise distance are never stored.

components.name: ZIP Room Authorization
components.description: Short-lived eligibility tokens from geofence verification gate write access to a specific ZIP Code room. Tokens expire; re-verification is required to re-enter after expiry. Browse access to public rooms requires no token and no location permission.
components.notes: No implementation authorized. Browse access does not require location permission or verification.

components.name: Real-Time Chat
components.description: WebSocket-based messaging for ZIP Code rooms. Covers message delivery, order guarantees, reconnection handling, and media attachment policy. The chat store is private and never committed to any public repository.
components.notes: No implementation authorized. Moderation must be production-ready before any public chat launch. Chat store is private infrastructure only.

components.name: Moderation and Trust-and-Safety
components.description: Report, block, and mute flows; moderation queue and action log; per-user and per-room rate limits; automated content signals. Community reports are labeled as unverified until independently confirmed by NYC In Focus editorial. Moderation is a launch requirement, not a post-launch addition.
components.notes: No implementation authorized. There is no 'launch now, add moderation later' path. Community reports must be labeled as unverified until independently confirmed.

components.name: Push Notifications
components.description: Opt-in per-topic notification delivery via APNs (iOS) and FCM (Android). Independent controls for ZIP chat, selected boroughs, event categories, Gold/Silver significance tiers, saved event reminders, breaking NYCIF coverage, and new stories. Rate-limited per topic and per user. Easy to disable from every surface.
components.notes: No implementation authorized. Notifications must be opt-in. The product must never rely on notification spam for retention.

components.name: NYC In Focus Website
components.description: Current active web presence hosting the public event map, editorial content, and borough pages. All changes require separate explicit authorization.
components.notes: All website changes require separate explicit authorization. The public map is curated and may intentionally show less than the operator/press God View.

components.name: iOS Application
components.description: Native iOS app delivering the three-panel experience: center map, left ZIP chat, right story feed. Press-and-hold navigation, swipe gestures, accessibility, and all device form factors. TestFlight testing required before any App Store submission.
components.notes: No implementation authorized. No App Store submission without completing Milestone 14 privacy, safety, and store-readiness checks.

components.name: Android Application
components.description: Native Android app delivering the same three-panel experience as iOS. Google Play internal track testing required before any store submission.
components.notes: No implementation authorized. No Play Store submission without completing Milestone 14 privacy, safety, and store-readiness checks.

components.name: Editorial Feed and WordPress Integration
components.description: Right-panel story feed consuming NYCIF editorial content from WordPress via the articles and media API. Story cards, photo and video, borough and category feeds, map pin deep links, and local room deep links. Editorial, community, and sponsored content are visually distinct.
components.notes: No implementation authorized. WordPress integration changes require separate authorization. Content types must never be visually ambiguous.

components.name: Widgets and Newsletter
components.description: Home-screen event widgets, lock-screen event previews, and NYCIF newsletter surface. Not authorized until the core iOS and Android applications complete Milestone 14.
components.notes: No timeline or authorization before Milestone 14 completes.

integrationPoints.notes: The API reads from the production event store only; it does not write to the pipeline.
Versioned API contract. Breaking changes require a new API version.
Website migration to the shared API is part of Milestone 8 scope.
Significance tier is included in the event API response. Tier computation is independent of commercial relationships.
Story feed pulls editorial content. Content-type labels (editorial, community, sponsored) are required in every response.
WordPress CMS publishes to the articles and media API. This integration is part of Milestone 13. Requires separate authorization.
Geofence service issues boolean eligibility result; ZIP room auth service issues the short-lived write token.
Chat write gate validates the short-lived room authorization token before allowing any post.
APNs delivery for iOS. Must be opt-in per topic. Rate-limited per topic and per user.
FCM delivery for Android. Must be opt-in per topic. Rate-limited per topic and per user.
Authenticated sessions enable saved events and personalized features.
An authenticated session is required before ZIP room authorization can issue a write token.

architectureDecisions.title: Single backend for all client surfaces
architectureDecisions.decision: One backend API serves the website, iOS app, Android app, widgets, newsletter, and future partner APIs.
architectureDecisions.rationale: A single backend avoids divergent data contracts, reduces duplication, and makes privacy and rate-limit policies enforceable in one place.
constraints: Breaking API changes require a new API version.
Existing clients must not be broken by internal platform changes.

architectureDecisions.title: Server-side geofence verification only
architectureDecisions.decision: User coordinates are sent to the server; a boolean eligibility result and a short-lived token are returned. Coordinates are never returned to the caller or stored beyond the verification request. Client-side polygon checks are not acceptable.
architectureDecisions.rationale: Client-side verification cannot be trusted. Returning coordinates to the client exposes them if the app is compromised or the network is intercepted.
constraints: Client-side polygon checks are not acceptable in any release.
Coordinates, movement history, and precise distance are never stored or returned.

architectureDecisions.title: Location permission requested at posting time only
architectureDecisions.decision: Precise location permission is requested only when a user attempts to post in a local room. Map browsing and room reading do not require location access. Background location is not requested in the initial release.
architectureDecisions.rationale: Requesting location at first launch increases rejection rates and erodes user trust. The product must earn location access at the moment it is clearly useful.
constraints: Background location is not required for the initial release.
Browsing the map and reading rooms must work without any location permission.

architectureDecisions.title: Moderation is a launch requirement
architectureDecisions.decision: Report, block, mute, rate-limit, moderation queue, action log, and contact mechanisms must be implemented and tested before any public chat launch. There is no 'launch now, add moderation later' option.
architectureDecisions.rationale: Public chat without moderation creates safety and legal risks. Community trust is a product asset easier to build than to repair after an incident.
constraints: No public chat launch without all moderation controls in place and tested.

architectureDecisions.title: Evidence-based event significance only
architectureDecisions.decision: Gold, Silver, and Bronze tiers are computed from measurable signals. No tier can be purchased or influenced by commercial relationships. Users may view the evidence behind any tier assignment.
architectureDecisions.rationale: Editorial credibility is the product's core trust asset. Paid significance tiers would destroy that credibility and risk mislabeling commercial placement as independent editorial assessment.
constraints: Sponsored placement uses a distinct label separate from significance computation.
Editorial selections use a distinct label separate from significance computation.
Users must be able to view why an event received its tier.

architectureDecisions.title: Chat store never in a public repository
architectureDecisions.decision: The chat database and all private user records — messages, verification events, moderation actions — are stored only in private infrastructure and are never committed to any public code repository.
architectureDecisions.rationale: User posts in geographic rooms are sensitive. Committing them to a public repository would violate user expectations and potentially applicable legal obligations.
constraints: This constraint applies to all user activity logs, moderation records, and location verification events.

nonNegotiableRules: No component writes to the production event store without explicit publish authorization.
Precise user coordinates are never exposed to other users or in any public API response.
Geofence verification is server-side only; client-side polygon checks are not acceptable.
Posting eligibility tokens expire; re-verification is required for re-entry after expiry.
Browse access to public rooms requires no token and no location permission.
The chat store and all private user records are never committed to any public repository.
Moderation, reporting, blocking, and contact mechanisms are required before any public chat launch.
Event significance tiers cannot be influenced by payment or commercial relationships.
Sponsored placement and editorial selections use distinct labels; neither is part of significance computation.
Every integration point and service boundary requires separate authorization before implementation begins.
No milestone automatically authorizes the next milestone, any production launch, or any app-store submission.
